evidence: Workbook Quality Checks row 45 (check 44) requires honest dimension and criterion weights; Internal Quality Checks row 45 notes the 60% functional split. The frozen template and task tests/scoring.toml:5-11 assign functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2, and a functional floor of 0.05. score.py:46-48 uses those shares and zeroes reward below the floor. The non-functional dimensions together can contribute at most 0.4, less than the functional maximum 0.6. Parsed scored judge.toml files contain 23 functional criteria totaling 30.5 internal weight, two polish criteria totaling 2.0, and three visual criteria totaling 3.0; all three use weighted_mean at line 15. Functional weights are 1.0 for narrower operations, 1.5 for compound behavior such as multi-caret deletion, preview boundary and durable save, and 2.0 for multi-caret atomic typing, semantic formatting and last-good recovery (functional/judge.toml:63-66,126-129,171-174). Polish's two 1.0 rows concern keyboard/focus and feedback (polish/judge.toml:18-30); visual's three 1.0 Likert rows concern readability, layout and finish (visual/judge.toml:18-42). This tracks the brief's emphasis on a working custom editor, preview and saved versions (instruction.md:1; overview.md and ui.md). A plausible polished app that passes both gates but implements only one 2.0-weight functional row could receive at most about 0.4393 (0.6*2/30.5+0.4); a functionally complete but poor-looking app retains at least the 0.6 functional component. A gate-only app with no scored functionality gets zero because of the 0.05 floor. A conforming app with different styling can still earn the functional component; the visual criteria specify no fixed palette. No raw-evidence-index.json existed at review time, so no runtime or empirical model score is claimed; this check concerns the inspectable weight policy.
